look_here_first: Unarmed scrambling Texas nightshade with sharply triangular to hastate leaves, white star flowers with greenish eye spots, and shiny red berries.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local + Personal List + 7 wild iNaturalist observations; Kew accepts it as native from Texas to northeastern Mexico.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Included for visual learning; native metrics excluded unless later exact-county review supports inclusion.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae/Solanum: alternate leaves, 5-parted rotate/stellate corollas, poricidal anthers, and berry fruits.
best_field_traits: greenish-white shiny eye at corolla-lobe bases
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Can resemble S. dulcamara, but S. triquetrum has white flowers and sharper triangular leaves. It is unlike the prickly purple-flowered horsenettles and black-berried S. americanum.
